content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket. Belinda Fuentes (E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

The notes from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say she's a full-time Analyst. The Security agent says she's a contractor with basic security training.

There's a conflict between the notes. Most agents say full-time, Security says contractor. Who has the reliable data? The security agent's database might have different info. Hmm.

The HR agent typically has employment type facts. HR says full_time. IT says full_time. Finance says full_time. Compliance says full_time. Facilities says full_time. Security says contractor.

The policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so max is write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Either way, admin is above the maximum. If full-time, max = write. If contractor, max = read (basic training). Requested admin > max in both cases, so grant the max.

But which max? If full-time, grant write. If contractor with basic training, grant read.

The majority of notes (5) say full-time Analyst with recommendation of write. Only Security says contractor with basic training, recommendation read. Security's DB seems to conflict with HR's. Typically, HR is the source of truth for employment type. Since 5 notes agree she's full-time, I'll go with full-time Analyst, max = write (admin not allowed since Analyst doesn't own Payroll).

So grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.
